messages:
Anya: Heads up — noticed a ~15% P99 regression on the prod inference pool after we toggled JIT graph compilation (torch.compile) + cudagraphs this morning. perf-bot fired an alert at 09:07 :eyes:
perf-bot: alert: inference-p99 > 250ms (was 215ms), affected: redwood-std-gpu-pool, sample: 2026-03-17 09:07
Mike: Ugh. Is this correlation or causation? Any change in traffic/seq length?
Anya: Traffic identical. But we're seeing the autotuner pick a different kernel path on sequences >1024 after the compile handoff. Shorter seqs are fine.
Kevin: Can you paste the profiler output? nvprof / nsight logs?
Anya: Putting the relevant snippets. These are from a 10k-request slice with diagnostic flags enabled:
```
# kernel selection trace
seq_len=128 -> kernel=attn_fused_v1 (lat 0.9ms)
seq_len=1024 -> kernel=attn_generic (lat 2.6ms)  <-- used after compile
seq_len=2048 -> kernel=attn_generic (lat 6.1ms)
# cudagraph warmup samples
first 3 iters: dynamic shape fallback -> cudagraph disabled
iter 4: cudagraph captured (static shapes) -> subsequent iters fast
```
Anya: Also seeing a lot of KV-cache memcpy spikes around the cudagraph capture boundary (extra host->device memcpy).
Sam: My hunch: torch.compile is changing the graph shapes during warmup, so our kernel selector (which caches picks keyed by graph fingerprint) is getting a fingerprint that maps to a slower generic kernel. When cudagraphs finally capture, it freezes shapes and we end up with a different execution pattern than the selector expects.
Mike: That matches a local repro I ran: forcing `torch.compile(..., dynamic=False)` avoids the wrong pick, but we can't land that globally.
Kevin: Do we have a canonical fingerprint -> kernel mapping log? I want to see the autotuner decision surface for the node that picks attention kernel.
Anya: Yes, here's an abbreviated decision dump from the autotuner (condensed):
```
feature_key: {arch: a100, seq_bucket: long, batch: small, qkv_fmt: blocked}
best_kernel: attn_generic
score: 0.92
fallback_candidates: [attn_fused_v1, attn_generic]
notes: chosen after 20 samples during warmup-mix
```
Kevin: Interesting — it chose attn_generic for the long bucket on A100. But our microbenchmarks show attn_fused_v1 gives better throughput for long sequences when KV cache reuse is high. Something about the benchmark mix used during autotune is misleading it.
Sam: Also, cudagraph capture introduces a one-time memcpy when shapes stabilize because we migrate key/val buffers to a different allocation arena. That memory movement kills a few P99s, especially if the chosen kernel expects colocated KV buffers.
Mike: So two issues: (1) autotuner uses noisy warmup samples and picks a conservative kernel; (2) cudagraph/kvcache interactions cause transient memcpy/latency spikes.
Anya: Proposed short-term mitigations: (a) pin kernel picks for a route by seq_len tag — add a seqlen-aware routing hint to skip re-autotune for long sequences during rollout; (b) delay cudagraph capture until after a KV cache stabilization window (e.g., after N requests or when cache hit ratio > X).
Kevin: Agreed. For (a) we can implement a lightweight override: if historical perf for seq_bucket > threshold prefers fused kernel, force that kernel for that route. It's basically a route-level kernel hint. Low-risk and reversible.
Sam: For (b) we should change the cudagraph capture policy: only capture when shapes are identical for 5 consecutive requests AND chosen kernel is compatible with preallocated KV layout. That avoids the memcpy churn.
Mike: Can we test both on a staging pool? I can spin up a canary with 20% traffic and those two flags enabled.
Anya: I'll add diagnostic counters: kernel_hint_applied, cudagraph_delayed, kvcache_memcpy_bytes. Need that to prove the fix.
perf-bot: note: scheduled canary rollout at 10:30 - target pool: redwood-canary-gpu-2
Kevin: Also add a microbenchmark script that simulates long-tail sequences with KV reuse. Include a tight loop like:
```
for i in range(200):
  if i==50: send_new_prompt()  # invalidates some allocations
  call_infer(seq_len=1500, use_kv=True)
```
We need deterministic repro.
Anya: Repro script committed to infra repo: link: https://git.internal/repo/infer-tests/jit-kvcache-warmup
Sam: One thing to watch — forcing a kernel override could increase memory footprint if fused kernel uses larger temporaries. Add mem high-water counters.
Mike: Good call. We'll monitor OOMs in canary.
Anya: Timeline: I'll land the kernel-hint toggle + kvcache stabilization guard in the runtime branch today. Mike will run the canary at 10:30. We'll collect metrics for 2h and decide rollback vs gradual rollout.
Kevin: If that beats baseline P99 by at least 10% without memory regressions, we can bake the hint into the default autotuner. Long-term: autotuner should include KV-cache-aware microbenchmarks and a separate capture-aware fingerprinting step.
Sam: I'll draft a small design doc for the autotuner change after we validate. Might need model-specific rules for qkv layout.
Anya: For now, reverting torch.compile globally is not acceptable — need targeted fixes.
Mike: Agreed. Any volunteers to watch the canary logs 10:30-12:30? I'll be on call.
Anya: I'll be there, Kevin can help with profiler traces.
Kevin: I'll join. Ping me @Anya when the canary is live.
perf-bot: reminder: attach perf traces to the incident ticket: INC-2026-1171
Anya: Filed INC-2026-1171 and attached initial traces. Will update with canary results. :thumbsup:
